sources.citation: Energizer HS/AS User Manual AU, 230224 — https://www.energizersolar.com/s/Energizer-HS-AS-User-Manual-AU_230224_LR.pdf (downloaded to scratchpad/ez-hsas.pdf)

transport: Battery link is CAN over RJ45 ('CAN (communicate with inverter, upgrade BMS)' is the only battery communication interface listed). Bit rate not stated. Inverter monitoring RS-485 exists per the product spec but no pinout, baud, framing, or slave ID is given in the manual for this series. Meter bus default Modbus addresses 1 (Meter1) and 2 (Meter2).
refutedOnReview: REFUTED. The cited source is real and I read all 50 pages (text layer + OCR of the image-only pages) of scratchpad/ez-hsas.pdf, but it contains no register map, so it cannot support a shared-register-map dialect at vendor-doc confidence.  What the manual does contain: §1.1 "Scope of Validity" names all ten models (HS-3.0/3.7/4.6/5.0/6.0, AS-3.0/3.7/4.6/5.0/6.0); §4 technical-data tables and §6.3 AC cable/breaker tabl
gotchas: Battery voltage range 80-480 V, recommended 300 VDC — this is a HIGH-VOLTAGE battery inverter, not a 12/24/48 V cabin device. Nothing in this line talks to a 48 V bank.
The AS variants are AC-coupled retrofit units with no PV input; pv-* metrics do not exist on them.
As with HS+, no register list is published by the vendor for any Force model.
This series is the AU/EU/DE line. No CSA/UL certification found.
unmappedReports: EPS/backup output power, grid import vs. export direction, battery charge/discharge current limit readback (40 A max charge, 40 A max discharge)
